items.question: Rule on this T4 finding.
items.artifact: SP\Ezek\tools\citation_sweep.py and SP\Ezek\tools\check_marks.py, PUNCTA arm (puncta_claim_numbers/_range_items via RANGE_NUM)
items.claim: R4(ii) order (1)'s parenthetical-after rule reads ANY C:V/C.V-shaped substring inside the directly-following parenthetical as a verse-number claim, with no check that the parenthetical is actually about puncta at all.
items.evidence: Constructed vector 'the puncta extraordinaria (cross-referenced at row R4.5 in the ledger)' is wrongly flagged in BOTH citation_sweep (ref form) and check_marks (prose form) as 'claims puncta extraordinaria but they stand only at MT 41:20 and MT 46:22 ... the claim names another verse' -- run live against the pinned tools in a private scratch copy, not merely reasoned from the regex.
items.how_verified: Subprocess run of citation_sweep.py and check_marks.py over constructed JSONL rows in my own private scratch (ezek_t4_9f21ab), same invocation pattern _test_zone_tools_ezek.py uses.
items.suggested_fix: Require the parenthetical's number to be paired with a mark-adjacent cue (e.g. only bind when the parenthetical contains nothing but a bare C:V/range and optional 'single-witness', or require a colon-form C:V distinguishable from a dotted id like 'R4.5' by anchoring the chapter to a plausible Ezek chapter 1-48 AND rejecting a leading letter run immediately before the digits). Likelihood in real rows: LOW-MEDIUM -- the campaign's own prose habitually cites ruling/row ids with a similar dotted shape (R4-ii, P10-008, CWO-EZ-10), so a writer referencing such an id inside a parenthetical placed directly after a puncta mention is a plausible, not merely theoretical, authoring pattern.

A C:V or C.V number is refused when a letter stands directly before its digits, so a dotted id such as 'R4.5' makes no verse claim, while 'Ezek.41.20', '(41:20)' and '41.20' still bind. The vectors are T4's decoy in both tools (it fails on the installed tools and passes when staged) and a dotted Ezek ref that still binds.

items.question: Rule on this T4 finding.
items.artifact: SP\Ezek\tools\citation_sweep.py puncta_negated() (shared by the PUNCTA arm and, via the same function, the CALENDAR-DATE arm's apposition/parenthesis logic)
items.claim: puncta_negated() only scans for a negation word BEFORE the mention's own position within its clause. A denial phrased with the negating word AFTER the target ('a dateline would be expected but none stands') is not recognized as a negation, so the CAL-1 apposition rule wrongly reads the preceding clause's number as an asserted dateline claim.
items.evidence: Constructed vector 'the unit opens at 45:18, where a dateline would be expected but none stands' is wrongly flagged 'claims a dateline at MT 45:18 - a calendar date with no year word is never a dateline', run live against the pinned citation_sweep.py in a private scratch copy. A control vector targeting an off-list verse ('45:17, and the dateline question is set aside') correctly stays GREEN, isolating the defect to the negation-direction gap rather than to the apposition number-matching itself.
items.how_verified: Subprocess run of citation_sweep.py over constructed JSONL rows in my own private scratch (ezek_t4_9f21ab).
items.suggested_fix: Extend puncta_negated() (or add a forward-looking variant used only by the apposition path) to also recognize a denial word in the clause immediately FOLLOWING the mention when the mention's own preceding clause is what supplies the apposition number -- i.e. when the apposition fallback fires, check both the number's own preceding clause AND the mention's own clause for a negator before accepting the claim as asserted. Likelihood in real rows: MEDIUM-HIGH specifically for MT 45:18, which TOOLKIT.md itself flags as the book's single most actively-discussed near-miss ('Watch MT 45:18 above all ... exactly the combination that reads like an oracle onset'); a primary or author explaining exactly why 45:18 is NOT a dateline is a natural and expected thing to write, and 'X would be expected but none stands' / 'X, though none is present' are ordinary English phrasings for that denial.
items.orchestrator_proposed_disposition: PROPOSED: staged in TOOLFIX-1. A mention also counts as a denial when a closed set of denial constructions follows it inside its own clause, read through a parenthetical opening directly after it. A bare later 'no', 'none of' and a non-final 'is missing' do not deny, so 'the dateline at 45:18 opens no new year' stays RED. A denial behind a comma stays outside the clause and stays RED, a disclosed residual. Vectors cover both directions in all three dateline readings and both puncta arms. You may prefer T4's broader rule (any later negator, on the apposition path only). Until an install lands, the primaries' hand-checkers treat a RED dateline flag on a 45:18 denial as a possible tool false positive and resolve it from the text.

P01-012's Qere אַרְבַּע at 7:2 is accent_stripped against the note's raw Qere and passes both HARD gates.
